title: Tenant-credit soft-deadline multiplexor with kernel suitability scoring
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: High tail latency under mixed tenant workloads when kernel suitability varies by request shape. Existing phase-splitting schedulers optimize for fairness or throughput but lack an economic signal across tenants, and they do not explicitly incorporate kernel probing signals. This ticket proposes a Tenant-credit soft-deadline multiplexor: a scheduler that assigns soft deadlines based on per-tenant credits and request urgency, and chooses phase splits guided by a lightweight kernel suitability score (kernel-probe feedback + shape heuristics). The goal is to reduce P99 latency for latency-sensitive tenants while preserving overall throughput and avoiding starvation of low-credit tenants.
design_decisions: 4) Multiplexor policy: combine soft-deadline urgency, tenant weight, and kernel suitability into a single scheduling rank: rank = w1*urgency + w2*tenant_weight + w3*kernel_suitability - w4*estimated_tokens_in_flight. We will expose w1..w4 as config knobs in runtime.
tradeoffs: - Cons: credit system adds state and tuning surface; kernel probing adds a small probe cost and complexity; rank weights require experimentation per cluster.
experiments: 1) Canary in a single low-latency cluster: enable tenant credits for 10% of traffic and measure P50/P95/P99 per-tenant. 2) Kernel probe overhead test: measure additional latency and throughput impact of lightweight probes on short requests. 3) Throughput regression test: run synthetic mixed-load with high-throughput long-seq jobs and latency-sensitive short-seq jobs to quantify trade-offs.
acceptance_criteria:
- 20% reduction in P99 for labeled latency-sensitive tenants vs baseline when tenant-credit policy enabled (no >5% drop in cluster throughput).
- Kernel probe overhead < 2% tail latency increase for probe-enabled requests.
- No tenant observed starvation for more than 30s under steady load.
- Config knobs documented and available in runtime config UI.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (dev): implement credit bookkeeping and rank function behind a feature flag, unit tests for fairness invariants.
Phase 2 (staging): enable kernel suitability probes and validate probe performance on staging clusters. Run synthetic experiments.
Phase 3 (canary): route 5-10% production traffic for non-critical tenants. Monitor P99 and throughput.
Phase 4 (gradual rollout): increase to 50% and tune weights, then full rollout for cluster with runtime-flag controls.
monitoring_and_metrics:
- Per-tenant P50/P95/P99 token latency and request latency.
- Kernel-switch frequency and average kernel-batch utilization.
- Tenant credit balances over time.
- Request probe success/failure and extra latency introduced by probes.
- Throughput (tokens/s) and GPU utilization per node.
